Paper: rule-based heuristics exclude trajectories that "exhibit failures in tool responses".

upstream_generation.tool_definitions: real MCP server specs crawled from GitHub and Smithery (third-party owners). Quote: "(2) excluding servers requiring third-party credentials (e.g., API keys) for tool invocation to maintain accessibility and reproducibility."
upstream_generation.user_queries: Quote: "we utilized five open-source LLMs (Mistral-Small, DevStral-Small, GPT-OSS, Kimi-K2, and Qwen3-32B) as task generators to construct synthetic tasks". Per-row generator: HF discussion #2, author: "Now it's in `synthetic_data_gen_configs` in metadata. Note that `\"step\": \"1.2\"` is for generating questions~"
upstream_generation.calls_trajectories: Quote: "we employed three LLMs from different families (GPT-OSS-120B, Kimi-K2, and Qwen3-32B) in combination with two agent frameworks (Qwen-agent and OpenAI-agent)"; card: "We include trajectories generated by Qwen3-32B, Kimi-K2, and GPT-OSS-120B, each stored under separate configurations."
upstream_generation.tool_responses: real MCP execution (Table 1: Tool Specs 'Real', Tool Response 'Executed')
upstream_generation.verification: Task judge: "We employed the Kimi-K2 model as the annotator" (6 Likert dimensions). Trajectory: "Rule-based heuristics exclude trajectories that fail to start the agent or connect successfully with remote MCP servers, do not contain tool calls, exhibit failures in tool responses, or contain local file system paths. We also validate whether the trajectory uses the required tools specified by the task in the correct sequence"; "We then employ GPT-OSS-120B as a judge to annotate each trajectory in terms of completeness and conciseness." Human-vs-judge Pearson correlation measured on 50 instances (Appendix C.1).

datasets.generator_terms: All named generators are open-weight with permissive terms: Mistral-Small-3.x / Devstral-Small (Apache-2.0), gpt-oss (Apache-2.0 + comply-with-law usage policy), Kimi-K2 (modified MIT, UI attribution only for >100M MAU or >$20M/month commercial products), Qwen3-32B (Apache-2.0). The pipeline config also lists openai/gpt-4.1 and x-ai/grok-3-mini as available endpoints; the paper says GPT-4.1 was only compared as a judge ("GPT-4.1 and Kimi-K2 achieve the highest overall correlation with human judgments. Considering cost efficiency, we deploy Kimi-K2 locally"). Whether any row was generated by a non-listed model: not established without reading per-row metadata.
datasets.contamination: No decontamination statement for BFCL, tau-bench, MCP-Universe or ACEBench. Quote: "We note that most servers in the benchmark require careful configurations and thus were not included in our data synthesis pipeline." (MCP-Universe). Not derived from BFCL.
datasets.availability: public, no gate. Large: ~21 GB download (sum of config download_size).
quality_notes: Card: "The data were collected between June and September 2025; therefore, tool responses may reflect events restricted to this period".
Card PII notice: "We have made a best-effort attempt to scan our datasets and remove PII using rule-based string replacements."
Ethics: "Given the case a legitimate owner requests removal of their content from our dataset, we will honor that request through a take down process available via our GitHub repository."
Quality labels are LLM-judge scores; paper's SFT subset used question quality and realism = 5, completeness and conciseness >= 4, desired tool use percentage = 1.0.
conditions: Ingest only rows whose metadata.synthetic_data_gen_configs names an allowlisted permissive model (Qwen3-*, gpt-oss-*, Kimi-K2*, Mistral-Small-3.x, Devstral-Small); reject anything else.
Keep Apache-2.0 attribution/NOTICE; honour takedown requests for MCP server content; treat tool responses as third-party web content that may contain residual PII (P15).
Recorded responses replay only when the teacher's call matches a recorded call; otherwise a live server (may be gone or changed) or a simulator is needed. Record which.
Prefer the 119,287-row SFT config or a metadata-filtered sample; do not move the full ~21 GB without a consumer (P8.4).
datasets.why: Permissive dataset license, all named task and trajectory generators are permissive open-weight models, tool specs are real, and tool responses are real executions. Remaining risks: per-row generator must be verified, third-party MCP content, time-bound responses.
